remaining_gaps: Item (1) directs that an Optical Manufacturing Industry Committee be created, with seven elected industry members and three non-voting members appointed by the Administrator, as a planning and fair-practice agency. This is an organizational command beside a code approval, a category SHARED_ANALYSIS.md item 5 leaves undecided and requires to be treated command by command. No held source shows whether or when the committee was constituted or when it ceased (a search of the held order texts finds the committee named only in EO 6325), so neither an exhausted-by-performance date nor a code-dependent end is established for item (1); applying the shared June 14, 1935 answer to it would force it.

The clause inventory (lead and item (1)) must be complete before a claim assembles, so the approval clause, whose end the shared analysis would give as 1935-06-14, cannot be filed alone. Needed: a held record of the committee's constitution and dissolution (an NRA administrative record or the code's administrative orders), or held text showing that the condition was only a term of the approval.

Own term and extension: EO 6877 runs 'until February 1, 1935'. EO 6955-A (February 1, 1935; held government printed copy jobs/hathi-gpo-orders/output/texts/EO_6955A.txt and the APP text) amended it 'to the following extent only' so that the Board administers paragraph 2 under the principles of EO 6877 'until thirty (30) days after the report of the Wool Textile Work Assignment Board is submitted to the President.' No held source shows when that report was submitted (EO 6878 of October 16, 1934 required recommendations before January 1, 1935 and EO 6930 of December 27, 1934 allowed 'a reasonable time after January 1, 1935'; neither records the submission). If the report was submitted before May 15, 1935 the rules ended before June 14, 1935; otherwise they ran to the repeal. The first end is therefore not established.

Item 1 directs the Textile Labor Relations Board (created by EO 6858) to appoint the Wool Textile Work Assignment Board and item 3 authorizes that Board to appoint district chairmen and issue rules: an appointment direction and an organizational delegation beside the code-administration rules. No held source shows when the Board was appointed or ceased, and EO 6878 (the same date) deals with the Cotton, Silk and Wool Work Assignment Boards together without saying whether it supersedes part of EO 6877. Each command needs its own end, and none is held.

Needed: a held record of the date the Wool Textile Work Assignment Board's report was submitted to the President, and a held record of the Board's appointment and operation, before a claim can state the first end of each clause.

Direction to the National Industrial Recovery Board to determine, after notice and hearing, which provisions of this code or of the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade Code (approved by EO 6321, October 3, 1933) prevail: a direction to an agency whose performance date is unknown. No held source shows that the Board held the hearing or made the determination, or when; if performed before June 14, 1935 the clause was exhausted by performance on that date, and if not, whether it lapsed with the repeal is a different question. Neither is established, and the Board's administrative orders are not among the held order texts.

Stay of Sections 2 and 3 of Rule 1 of Article VII and Rule 15 of Article VII 'pending the further order of the National Industrial Recovery Board': the order's own terms name a contingent earlier end. No held source shows whether the Board lifted the stay before June 14, 1935 (a Board order would be an administrative order, not an executive order, and none is held).

Stay of the words 'to participate in the selection of members of the National Code Authority or' in Section 13-(i)-2 of Article VI 'until such time as the National Code Authority is duly constituted and organized': a condition whose occurrence is not shown by any held source, so whether the stay ended before June 14, 1935 is not established.

The 60-day stay as to members of the Motor Vehicle Retailing Trade has a certain own-terms end (about March 19, 1935, with a one-day variance by day-count convention) but a claim cannot be filed while the other three clauses lack ends. Needed: held NIRB orders or notices showing the determination, any lifting of the Rule stays, and the constitution of the National Code Authority.

The stay of Sections 2 and 3 of Article VII and Rule 14 of Article VIII runs 'pending the further order of the National Industrial Recovery Board'. No held source shows whether the Board issued a further order lifting the stay before June 14, 1935 (a Board order would be an administrative order, and none is held; a search of the held order texts finds the code only in EO 6952-A). So the stay clause's first end lies somewhere between January 24, 1935 and June 14, 1935 and is not established, and an inventory split into approval and stay is incomplete without it.
Needed: a held NIRB order or notice showing whether and when the stay was lifted, or held text showing that the Board issued none before the repeal.
